name: Restricted bucket and battery restriction settings
plain: The user can set an app to Unrestricted, Optimized or Restricted; unused apps can fall into Restricted.
meaning: The strongest user lever over background activity. Restricted means one 10 minute job session a day, almost no alarms, and no network; people rarely change it, so defaults shape reach.

android.persistence: Restricted bucket after 45 days (Android 12) or 8 days (Android 13+) of no interaction, or excessive broadcasts or bindings in 24 h
android.store_policy: Play: battery opt-out prompts only for allowed use cases
android.note: Exempt: companion apps, device owner, VPN, active widgets, USE_EXACT_ALARM holders, user chosen Unrestricted. Restricted bucket: one 10 min job session per day, 1 alarm per day

ios.prompt_ui: Background App Refresh toggle per app and globally; Low Power Mode
ios.note: Off disables background fetch and silent push handling for that app

limits.headline: Can only run in the background as much as your battery setting allows
limits.user_action: You open Settings, then Battery, and set the app to Unrestricted, Optimized or Restricted
can: Run freely in the background if you pick Unrestricted on Android
Run background tasks on iPhone if Background App Refresh is on
Ask you to loosen the limit when it needs more room
cannot: Override your choice; Restricted allows very little, about one short job a day
Run background fetch or silent push handling on iPhone when that app's refresh is off
Keep running if the system moves an unused app into the Restricted bucket on Android
limits.reach_label: Only what your battery setting allows
limits.differs: Android has three battery choices per app plus an automatic Restricted bucket. iPhone has a Background App Refresh switch and Low Power Mode.

story.what_it_is: You can set each app to unrestricted, optimized or restricted to control how much it runs in the background.

marketing.name: Battery settings
marketing.pitch: Google explains battery tools in Android settings, including how to limit apps that use too much power in the background.

story.for_you: You can open Battery settings and cap any app. A restricted app gets almost no background time, so it may stop alerts. Most people never touch it, so the default decides what happens.
story.for_makers: Makers know most users stay on the default, so reach depends on it. Some apps ask people to switch to Unrestricted for reliable alarms or tracking, which also costs more battery.

use_cases.example: A run tracker asks you to choose Unrestricted so it can record a full marathon.
A glucose monitor companion app is allowed to run freely so alerts for lows are never missed.
A chat app warns that alerts will be late while it is set to Restricted.
A baby monitor or door camera app is given unrestricted use so alerts come on time.
A game with timed events loses its reminder alerts after the phone moves it to Restricted.
A calendar app that adds a reminder at the right minute needs relaxed battery rules to be on time.

risks: Apps may nag you to remove limits
story.android_note: Settings offer Unrestricted, Optimized and Restricted. Restricted gets one short job session per day.
story.ios_note: iOS has a Background App Refresh switch per app and Low Power Mode, which is simpler.

technical_bounds: Apps can detect it but not override it

history.change: Idle threshold cut to 8 days; FGS task manager
Apps whose tasks time out too often can move to Restricted
